muse_spark_1.3/001: The strategy is center control with forced win/block and time limited alpha-beta. All 49 winning lines in 3x3x3 are precomputed as bit-masks on 27 bits. Immediate winning moves are taken, single opponent wins are blocked. Otherwise the center (13 lines) is taken, corners second. Remaining positions are searched with iterative deepening negamax with alpha-beta, move ordering by attacking/blocking potential and line counts, exponential evaluation counting 1 and 2 in-a-row, extra bonus for forks/double threats, faster wins preferred, breadth limited to top moves on deep plies to stay under 1s, always falling back to a legal move.
muse_spark_1.3/002: The strategy is center control with forced win/block and depth limited alpha-beta. All 49 winning lines are precomputed as 27-bit masks for fast win test and evaluation. Immediate winning moves are taken and single opponent wins are blocked. Otherwise the position is searched with negamax, iterative deepening, static move ordering by number of lines through a cell, win-shortcut and transposition table under a 0.85s deadline, preferring faster wins and delayed losses. Evaluation counts open lines with exponential weight for 2-in-a-row, slightly larger for defence, which automatically values center, corners and forks.
muse_spark_1.3/003: Strategy is center-dominated tactical search with bitboards. All 49 winning lines are precomputed. Immediate wins are taken, immediate losses blocked. Opening takes center, then corners. Middlegame uses iterative-deepening negamax with alpha-beta, forced-block pruning (single opponent threat forces the reply, double threat is terminal loss), immediate-win cutoff, quiescence on threats, and a line-potential evaluation (2-in-row =100, 1-in-row=1) that naturally values forks. Move ordering by evaluation + line-count keeps search within time and always falls back to a legal move.
muse_spark_1.3/004: Strategy is center control plus forced win/block with time-limited iterative deepening negamax. All 49 winning lines of 3x3x3 are precomputed as 27-bit masks for fast win check and evaluation. Policy first takes immediate win, then mandatory block, then searches. Search uses bitboards, win check only on lines through last move, static evaluation counting open lines (1->1, 2->100) from side-to-move perspective, move ordering by line-count (center first, corners next) with alpha-beta and transposition-free negamax. Iterative deepening from depth 2 up to full solve in endgame respects ~0.9s deadline and always falls back to a legal empty cell.
muse_spark_1.3/005: The strategy is center domination plus tactical search. Center belongs to 13 of 49 lines, corners to 7, so taking center when free is forced. Immediate wins are taken and immediate losses are blocked by sum check on all lines. Otherwise the position is searched with minimax alpha-beta. Line counts for the 49 winning lines are maintained incrementally, evaluation counts unblocked lines with exponential weights for 2-in-a-row threats, slightly higher for opponent to force blocks, plus small positional bonus. Moves are ordered by offensive plus defensive potential to get cutoffs and find forks, non-root nodes are beamed to top moves when branching is large, and iterative deepening under a time budget keeps the best move from the last completed depth, guaranteeing a legal move in under 1s.
